questions.text: Tell me about a time you collaborated closely with another developer on a challenging feature. How did you divide the work and keep your code in sync?
Describe a group software project where teammates had very different coding styles or skill levels. How did you help the team work effectively together?
rubric_hints: Concrete steps like pairing or shared standards

questions.text: Tell me about a time a teammate was falling behind on a shared engineering deliverable. How did you handle the situation?
rubric_hints: How work was reprioritized or supported

questions.text: Give me an example of when pair programming or a working session with a teammate helped you solve a problem much faster than working alone.
Describe a time you had to integrate your code with an API or component written by someone else, and it did not behave as expected.
Tell me about a time you contributed to improving your team's engineering workflow, such as documentation, testing, or deployment.
Have you ever worked on a project where someone else's code broke the build or main branch right before a demo? What did you do?
Tell me about a time you received help from a senior engineer or teammate that unblocked you. How did you prepare before asking?
rubric_hints: Clear summary of context when asking
What you took away for future work

questions.text: Describe a project where your team had to coordinate across multiple time zones or conflicting schedules. How did you stay aligned?
Tell me about a time you stepped outside your assigned tasks to support a teammate or unblock the broader project.
Tell me about a time you strongly disagreed with a teammate on a technical design or architecture choice. How did you resolve it?
rubric_hints: Alignment and commitment to final decision

questions.text: Describe a time you received harsh or frustrating feedback during a code review. How did you respond?
Tell me about a time you had to push back on a teammate's pull request because of quality, performance, or security concerns.
rubric_hints: Respectful tone and explanation of why

questions.text: Have you ever compromised on a technical approach you believed was better for the sake of the team or timeline? What happened?
Describe a situation where two teammates were deadlocked on how to implement a feature. What role did you play?
rubric_hints: Reframing around user or system goals

questions.text: Tell me about a time you realized mid-discussion that your proposed technical solution was wrong and a teammate's was better.
Tell me about a time you had to deliver constructive criticism to a peer about their code quality or engineering habits.
rubric_hints: Focus on behavior/code rather than person

questions.text: Describe a time when a code review caught a subtle bug in your work before it reached production. What did that teach you?
Have you ever disagreed with a senior engineer or team lead about how to solve a problem? How did you handle that conversation?
Tell me about a time friction in team communication slowed down development. What did you do to fix it?
rubric_hints: Initiative to clarify norms or channels

questions.text: Tell me about the hardest bug you have ever had to track down. How did you isolate the root cause?
Describe a time an application or service you worked on failed in production or during a live demo. How did you respond under pressure?
Tell me about a time you encountered an intermittent or hard-to-reproduce bug. How did you go about diagnosing it?
Give me an example of a performance bottleneck you identified and fixed in a codebase. How did you measure the improvement?
Describe a time you had to jump into an unfamiliar or poorly documented codebase and fix an urgent issue.
Tell me about a time your first attempt to fix a bug actually made things worse or revealed a deeper issue. What did you do next?
rubric_hints: Quick recognition and rollback if needed

questions.text: Describe a problem where you realized the bug was not in your code, but in an external library, environment, or configuration.
rubric_hints: How you proved the root cause

questions.text: Tell me about a time you automated a repetitive manual task or built an internal tool to save your team time.
Walk me through a time you solved a complex technical problem by breaking it down into smaller, testable parts.
Tell me about a time you noticed a potential reliability or security risk before anyone else did. What actions did you take?
Tell me about a time you made a mistake in your code that impacted your team or users. How did you handle it?
Describe a time you took ownership of a task or bug that technically belonged to no one else.
Tell me about a project or feature you owned from initial idea all the way to deployment or final delivery.
Give me an example of a time you underestimated the complexity of an engineering task. How did you recover?
Tell me about a time you accidentally deleted data, broke a test environment, or pushed a bad commit. What happened next?
Describe a situation where you spotted technical debt that nobody was prioritizing. What did you do about it?
Tell me about a time you shipped a feature and later realized users were using it differently than you expected.
Tell me about a time you committed to a deadline and realized halfway through that you might miss it.
Describe a time you had to clean up or refactor messy code that you yourself wrote earlier.
Give me an example of a time you went above and beyond to ensure the quality of a release.
rubric_hints: Attention to edge cases and testing

questions.text: Tell me about a time you were given a vague ticket or open-ended engineering requirement. How did you turn it into an actionable plan?
Describe a project where the requirements changed significantly halfway through development. How did you adapt?
Tell me about a time you had to make a technical decision without having all the information you wanted.
Give me an example of when scope creep threatened a project deadline. How did you help keep the project on track?
Tell me about a time you built a quick prototype or proof of concept to test an uncertain idea before committing to a full build.
rubric_hints: How findings shaped the real solution

questions.text: Describe a situation where you had to design a solution while key dependencies from another team or API were not ready yet.
Tell me about a time a stakeholder asked for a feature that seemed simple on the surface, but was technically complex underneath.
Have you ever worked on a project that was pivoted or cancelled after you had already invested significant effort? How did you handle it?
Describe a time you had to figure out edge cases that were not mentioned in the specification.
Tell me about a time you had to choose between shipping something imperfect now or waiting to build a cleaner solution.
Tell me about a time you were juggling multiple urgent bugs or feature tasks at once. How did you decide what to tackle first?
Describe a tight deadline you faced on a software project. How did you organize your work to meet it without sacrificing stability?
Tell me about a time you had to say no to a request or defer a feature because there was not enough time.
Give me an example of when you spent too much time perfecting a small detail instead of focusing on the bigger picture.
Describe how you break down a large multi-week engineering feature into daily or sprint-sized tasks.
Tell me about a time an unexpected high-priority issue interrupted work you were already behind schedule on.
Describe a time you recognized early that a project plan was unrealistic and spoke up about it.
Tell me about how you stay productive and avoid burnout during crunch periods like hackathons, exams, or release weeks.
Give me an example of a time you had to balance fixing lingering bugs against building new user-facing features.
Tell me about a time you missed a deadline or personal milestone. What caused it and what changed in your process afterward?
Tell me about a significant technical decision you made between two competing technologies, frameworks, or libraries.
rubric_hints: How the choice held up in practice

questions.text: Describe a time you chose a simpler, boring solution over a more complex or trendy one. Why?
Tell me about a time you designed a feature with scalability or future extensibility in mind.
Have you ever over-engineered a solution and later wished you had kept it simpler? Walk me through what happened.
Tell me about a time you decided to build something in-house versus using an existing third-party library or API.
rubric_hints: Build vs buy trade-offs (time, reliability, cost)

questions.text: Describe a time you had to balance code readability and maintainability against raw execution speed.
Tell me about a time you refactored a tightly coupled module to make it easier to test or maintain.
Describe a time you had to migrate data or update a schema without breaking existing functionality.
Tell me about how you decide how much automated testing a new feature needs before shipping it.
Give me an example of a design decision you made early in a project that you would change if you started over today.
Tell me about a time you had to learn a completely new programming language or framework very quickly for a project.
Describe the most valuable piece of constructive feedback you have received from a mentor, manager, or professor.
Tell me about a time you were stuck on a technical problem for hours. How did you eventually get unstuck?
rubric_hints: Knowing when to step back or change tactics
How you researched or asked for help

questions.text: Describe a technical topic or concept that took you a long time to truly understand, and how it finally clicked.
Tell me about a time you stepped out of your technical comfort zone, such as a backend developer doing frontend or vice versa.
How do you keep your software engineering skills sharp outside of required classes or day-to-day tickets?
Tell me about a time a tool, workflow, or AI assistant you relied on gave you misleading output or failed. How did you catch it?
Describe a time you had to unlearn an old habit or outdated practice when joining a new team or codebase.
rubric_hints: Understanding why the new way existed

questions.text: Tell me about a project that did not turn out the way you hoped. What was your biggest takeaway?
Describe a time you actively sought out feedback on your work before waiting for a formal review.
Tell me about a time you had to explain a complex technical issue or constraint to a non-technical stakeholder.
Describe a time you worked closely with a designer or product manager to refine a feature before or during implementation.
Tell me about a miscommunication on a project that caused wasted work. How did you help clear it up?
Give me an example of technical documentation, a design doc, or a README you wrote that made a real difference for others.
Tell me about a time you had to present or demo your technical work to a group. How did you prepare?
Describe a time you had to deliver bad news about a delay, bug, or technical limitation to a manager or client.
rubric_hints: Bringing proposed solutions, not just problems

questions.text: Tell me about a time you used data, benchmarks, or a user story to convince others to adopt your idea.
Describe a situation where you realized two teams were using the same terms to mean different things.
Tell me about how you keep teammates updated on your progress without overwhelming them with noise.
Describe a time you gathered feedback directly from users or testers and turned it into code changes.
Tell me about a time you took the lead on organizing a group software project when no formal leader was assigned.
Describe a time you mentored or helped onboard a newer student or teammate onto a codebase.
rubric_hints: Empowering them rather than doing it for them

questions.text: Tell me about a project or technical improvement you initiated on your own without being asked.
Describe a time you motivated a discouraged or stressed team during a difficult stretch of a project.
Tell me about a time you delegated or handed off part of your work to someone else. How did you make sure it succeeded?
Give me an example of a decision you made as a project lead that turned out to be unpopular at first.
Tell me about a software project you are most proud of building. What made your contribution meaningful?
Describe a time you helped set engineering standards, such as linting, Git branching, or code review checklists, for a team.
Tell me about a time you had to make a tough call between helping a teammate and finishing your own critical work.
Looking back at your recent engineering experiences, what kind of team environment brings out your best work, and how do you contribute to creating it?
rubric_hints: Concrete habits you bring to a team
